focus_area_title: Focus on the Basics: Improve your Communication Skills
content_text_body:
Team members often report frustration with their manager's poor communication skills or the inability of the manager to foster good communication practices on the team. The objective is to learn how to communicate more effectively, as well as create a culture of trust, respect, and mutual understanding across the team. 

### Why is it important?

By learning how to communicate more effectively, you will gain greater understanding of your own and others' perspectives; ensure team members have the information they need to do their jobs well; and foster more honest and open two-way conversations. Establishing good communication behaviors and expectations improves the experience of each team member, as well as overall team effectiveness.

### Learn these key communication skills
Keep this list of leadership communication "Do's and Don't" below handy and regularly practice these behaviors. Ask for feedback from a trusted colleague on how you are doing and ways to improve. 

#### Leadership Communication Do's and Don'ts

##### Do these things

**Ensure clarity**  
Your team is more likely to understand your message if you use language they relate to. You also want to use variety in your speech (tone, volume, and speed) to keep them engaged and to create emphasis where needed. At the same time, you want to be simple, direct and succinct.

**Create intimacy**  
Have honest, candid conversations with your team. Get personal, be trustworthy and be a [good listener](Glint_Leadership_Tips_for_Being_a_Better_Listener). Show a sincere interest in what's happening for them, both on and off the job. [Practice using empathy](Glint_Manager_How_to_Lead_with_Empathy
) when communicating with your team, and keep conversations confidential.

**Facilitate interactivity**  
Choose dialog over monolog. Make sure each person in the conversation gets a chance to actively participate. Ask questions to inspire ideas and inputs, and respond where it feels natural. This is especially important when solving problems and making decisions as a team. 

One-way directives should be reserved for times of confusion, or when efficiency is the most important goal. Although it can be effective, when overused, the directive style of communication can lead to complacency on the part of your team who may adopt an "I just do what they tell me" attitude.

**Foster inclusion**  
Ask your team to share their ideas, tell stories about themselves and their work. Create opportunities for team members to learn more about each other. Strive to use an open and accepting communication style, both verbally and nonverbally, so that all members of the team feel included.

##### Don't do these things

**Multitasking**  
Give what you're doing your full attention. Don't check your messages or try to read a report at the same time.

**Overcomplicate the message**  
Whether it's a written or verbal message, keep it simple.

**Be negative**  
Avoid harsh criticism, complaints, and gossip, and instead make sure to communicate in an open, honest, and positive manner.

**Avoid difficult conversations**  
The best way to handle a difficult message is to do it directly, preferably live and face to face. Don't hide behind technology. If you don't directly address the issue with employees, you are not giving them a chance to have a conversation with you-to respond, to react, to ask questions and clarify. 

**Put employees on the defensive**  
Avoid dominating the discussion, insisting on getting your two cents into every conversation.

### Create a feedback loop with your team
Ask your team to give you feedback on a regular basis on how well you are communicating and supporting effective communication practices on the team. Ask what you should continue doing, and what to do differently to be more effective.
